## Pokemon data

The dataset used here is sourced from {pokemon} ([CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/package=pokemon) \| [github](https://github.com/williamorim/pokemon)), an R package, and was put together by [Frank Hull](https://github.com/frankiethull).

```{r}
#load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(cowplot) #to add pic to plot
library(magick)
library(ggthemr)
library(ggrepel) #to label some points
```

```{r}
# Using R
# Option 1: tidytuesdayR R package 
## install.packages("tidytuesdayR")

tuesdata <- tidytuesdayR::tt_load('2025-04-01')
pokemon_df <- tuesdata$pokemon_df
```

```{r}
#subset blissey for good plot, to highlight that data point
blissey <- pokemon_df |> 
  filter(pokemon=="blissey")
```

```{r}
#plotting
ggthemr_reset() #reset usual theme for plots I use
theme_set(theme_cowplot())

#bad plot
notgood <- ggplot(pokemon_df, mapping = aes(x=base_experience, y=attack)) +
  geom_text(aes(label=base_experience), color="deeppink1") +
  labs(title="who to farm", y="biggest muscles", x="much exp") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim=c(0, 1000)) + #change y axis
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(1,23,789)) + #manual breaks
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=c(0)) +
  theme(axis.title = element_text(angle = 27, colour =  "pink"),
        plot.title = element_text(colour =  "pink", angle=12),
        panel.grid.major = element_line("pink"),
        panel.border = element_rect("pink"),
        axis.line = element_line("pink"),
        axis.text = element_text(color = "pink"))

#add blissey picture
ggdraw() +
  draw_plot(notgood)+
  draw_image(here("goodplot-badplot","242MS6.png"))

ggsave(here("goodplot-badplot","Outputs","horribleplot.png"))

```

This is an example of a bad plot using the Pokemon dataset from Tidy Tuesday. First, the actual data points are very hard to see in the plot - they are obscured by this large image of Blissey and the y-axis goes up too high so the points are all scattered together. Each data point is also labeled by text/numbers instead of smaller dots which also makes it hard to see.

Next, both the plot title and the axes titles are hard to read - they are either angled weirdly or in a harder to see color. The x-axis has no tick marks, while the y-axis has three breaks put in at seemingly random increments. All of the actual titles donʻt give any actual information on what they represent nor units of measure for the axis titles.

```{r}
#set a nicer looking theme to use for the good plot
ggthemr("dust")

#create better plot with the same data
betterplot <- ggplot(pokemon_df, mapping = aes(x=base_experience, y=attack)) + 
  geom_point(size=1) +
  labs(title="Blissey: The Best Pokemon to Farm", x="Base Experience", y="Attack Points", subtitle = "Base Experience by Attack Points plotted of 949 Pokemon") +
  geom_point(data = blissey, color="blue", shape = "square") +
  geom_label_repel(data=blissey, aes(label = pokemon), #from ggrepel package
                   box.padding   = 0.35, 
                   point.padding = 0.5,
                   segment.color = 'grey50')

betterplot
ggsave(here("goodplot-badplot","Outputs","betterplot.png"))
```

Here is a much better plot showing 949 pokemon plotted by their Attack Points and Base Experience. The titles and caption are much more informative and you can more clearly see the spread of the data points here. Finally, the data point for Blissey, the pokemon of interest, is highlighted in a way that is noticeable but does not get in the way of the other data points.
